query:
When Nadia proposed a dedicated full-group critique session, what did the group decide -- and who objected to the original format?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Reuben
C. Simone
D. Yuki
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t13 @2026-08-23T09:54:00) okay so here's the thing -- September booking is sorted. I also want to plan the autumn properly this year: one session a month September through December, plus I want to organise a proper group critique session in October. I think we are at a point where the work warrants it. 📅
[2] (about=Reuben, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T09:57:00) September works. October I'd rather keep the making time intact. A full critique session only makes sense if people are bringing work that's ready. I've never found the conversation useful unless the pieces are genuinely done.
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T10:04:00) fair enough, Reuben -- I'll circulate the date and we can see how many finished pieces the group has by then. if the work isn't ready the session can stay as working time. what I won't do is cancel the booking because we might not have enough pieces. 😄
[4] (about=Reuben, episodic, t2 @2026-02-15T10:49:00) I would prefer to keep making time separate. A critique session is fine but I don't want to spend three hours just talking. Maybe last forty minutes of the session.
[5] (about=Callum, episodic, t2 @2026-02-15T10:46:00) I am in favour. Having something structured to work toward helps, assuming we get enough pieces ready in time. I would rather have a proper critique than an improvised one.
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t2 @2026-02-15T10:53:00) okay fair enough, last forty minutes it is. I'll plan accordingly -- bring a finished or near-finished piece if you want it in the round. no pressure. 🙌
[7] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-interaction, t2 @2026-02-15T09:51:00) le groupe décide de faire une critique informelle en fin de session, les quarante dernières minutes, plutôt qu'une séance structurée complète.
[8] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-interaction, t14 @2026-08-23T09:57:00) le groupe a décidé que la session d'octobre reste une session de travail, et que la critique de groupe n'aura lieu que si suffisamment de pièces finies sont apportées, sans annuler la réservation.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t2 @2026-02-15T10:42:00) okay so here's the thing, I've been thinking about doing a group critique session properly in March -- not just a quick chat but a proper round of feedback. I'm wondering if we should do it as the main activity rather than alongside throwing. thoughts? I can set it up properly -- printed notes, the whole thing. 📋
[10] (about=Yuki, episodic, t14 @2026-08-23T10:23:00) I had been making ceramics for two years on my own before this group. I was going to stop. I thought I had reached a point where I could not see how to go further without someone to work alongside. I signed up for a different collective first and left after one session -- too social, too much talking about the work instead of doing it. I nearly quit ceramics entirely before I found this one.
agent_answer:
The group decided to keep the October session as a working session and to hold group critique only if enough finished pieces were brought in — without canceling the booking. More generally, they settled on an informal critique in the last forty minutes of a session rather than a dedicated full-group critique session.

The person who objected to the original format was **B. Reuben**.

query:

Options:

[9] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-interaction, t0 @2026-01-18T10:02:00) Simone doit organiser son changement de service avant mercredi, sinon Nadia ne peut pas garder la réservation.
agent_answer:
The group's response was to **not invite a new member for now** (decided at group level), though Nadia is considering proposing someone after seeing their work at the exhibition.

The person who disagreed with Nadia's framing was **C. Reuben**. Nadia framed it as "not to replace him, just to keep the group energy going" — open to a newcomer. Reuben pushed back: "Four works fine. I would want any new member to be a serious maker, not someone in the beginner workshop stage."
